senses.definition: (transitive) To draw or let out wholly; to drain completely.
examples: The water was exhausted out of the well.
Moisture of the earth is exhausted by evaporation.

senses.definition: (transitive) To empty by drawing or letting out the contents.

quotes.text: It takes approximately 8 to 9 minutes to exhaust the tank of air and fill it with water.

senses.definition: (transitive, literally, figuratively) To use up; to deplete, drain or expend wholly, or use until the supply comes to an end.
examples: My grandfather seemingly never exhausts his supply of bad jokes.
I exhausted my strength walking up the hill.

senses.definition: (transitive) To tire out; to wear out; to cause to be without any energy.

quotes.text: It is a branch that climbs for 11½ miles into the picturesque Wealden hills until, apparently exhausted by the effort, it terminates a mile short of the village of Hawkhurst.
quotes.reference: 1960 March, H. P. White, “The Hawkhurst branch of the Southern Region”, in Trains Illustrated, page 170:

examples: That subject has already been exhausted.

senses.definition: (transitive, chemistry) To subject to the action of various solvents in order to remove all soluble substances or extractives.
examples: to exhaust a drug successively with water, alcohol, and ether
